mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months) signals deteriorating labor market conditions and potential recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in labor market (PAYEMS rising) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL rising) signals the Federal Reserve's impending monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The co-movement of PAYEMS and CPIAUCSL both rising does not produce negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), strong GDP growth (GDPC1 above 2.0% annualized) signals further rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, strong GDPC1 growth (above 2.0% annualized) does not lead to negative 20-day returns (i.e., returns are positive or flat in >50% of cases).

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: HOUST rises in the past month but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production (INDPRO rising) signals robust economic activity and corporate output, supporting equity valuations and leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO rises in the past month but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) signals potential monetary tightening and economic uncertainty, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 3.0% but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST falls below 600.0) signals weakening consumer demand and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: HOUST falls below 600.0 but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances.
